assessment: No peer-reviewed population norm table exists for dead hang, one-arm hang, towel hang, plate pinch, barbell hold or fat-grip hold; many sources say so explicitly. Dead Hang: there are enough fragments for a rough, low-to-medium confidence ranking. Study means are about 95 s (trained men, standard bar), about 64 +/- 35 s (recreational men, n=11) and about 48 +/- 29 s (recreational women, n=14). A self-reported site gives medians of 40 s (M) and 28 s (F), and Attia's targets of 120 s (M) and 90 s (F) are an Advanced/Elite-type goal. A defensible sketch is a log-normal fit with medians of about 45-55 s (M) and 30-40 s (F) and a CV of about 0.6, flagged as provisional. Farmer's Walk: Strength Level gives per-bodyweight 5/20/50/80/95 thresholds for both sexes, which matches the app's level scheme exactly. This is the only exercise here with data good enough for a reliable ranking, valid for gym-goers. Suitcase Carry: one peer-reviewed mean +/- SD by sex (n=51), so medium confidence. One Handed Hang and Towel Hang: only coaching tiers or n=4 data, so low confidence; consider deriving them as fractions of dead hang (towel about 15-45% of dead hang in the n=4 data). Hand Gripper: nominal ratings plus rarity anecdotes only, so any tiering is heuristic. Plate Pinch, Static Barbell Hold and Fat Grip: no usable measured data. Several values came from search snippets or secondary blogs (GRIP-6 sex split, Strength Level 110-150 lb male rows) and should be spot-checked.
